evidence.field: file description, stated identity, source attribution, and license
evidence.text: The Commons page identifies 干-seal.svg as a vector depicting 干 in Shuowen seal-script style and lists several character databases as sources, including Sinica, Hanziyuan, and CUHK. It specifically traces the picture to Hanziyuan image s01611. It states that the vector representation is public domain and that attribution is appreciated but not required. This is a modern vector representation of a received seal-style form, not a dated artifact or evidence for the graph’s origin.
evidence.title: File:干-seal.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: file description, stated identity, date limitation, and license
evidence.text: The page identifies 干-oracle.svg as a vector depicting 干 in oracle-script style and states that it is public domain, with attribution appreciated but not required. It lists character databases as sources. The file is a modern redraw, uploaded in 2016; Commons marks it as needing a time period. It does not identify a specific inscription or securely date the form, so it should not be presented as a verified Shang artifact glyph.
evidence.title: File:干-oracle.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.field: 甲骨部件分析; formation, usage examples, competing account
evidence.text: The database interprets the oracle-bone and bronze graph as a shield, sometimes with upper feather decoration, and connects the defensive sense with that object. It reports an oracle-bone defensive example in 合集 28059, 弜令戍干衛, and bronze 豦簋 干戈 for the weapon sense; it also cites 毛公鼎 干吾王身 for a defensive use. It reports Xu Zhongshu’s alternative that some oracle-bone 干 forms are variants of 單 depicting a forked hunting implement. These are dictionary and scholarly interpretations; the page’s text and linked image slots were inspected, but no artifact glyph image was independently examined.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oraclePiece 干

evidence.text: The article identifies the mid-Western Zhou 豦簋 inscription as the earliest securely identifiable 干 in its account. It describes that form as a round shield with a forked upper part. Later Western Zhou forms regularize the round feature to a short horizontal stroke; this form continues through later script traditions, while the upper fork is changed to a shorter horizontal stroke by Eastern Han. The article presents proposed earlier Shang identifications separately as debated proposals.
evidence.title: 商周時期的防護裝具與兵器：甲、冑、干、盾（四） — CASE 報科學

evidence.source: 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.field: Western Zhou bronze readings and identification debate
evidence.text: Su Jianzhou reviews disputes over particular bronze forms and readings, including distinctions among 干, 盾, and other graphs. He compares paired inscription contexts, including 豦簋 “介胄干戈,” to support identifying related forms as 干. This reinforces that the shield interpretation has substantial support while showing that the reading of particular forms has been contested.
evidence.title: 蘇建洲：西周金文“干”字再議

evidence.text: The page for Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg returned a cache miss when opened. Its depiction, provenance, original image URL, and reuse terms were therefore not verified, so I cannot recommend it as an image on the basis of this lookup.

search_audit.query: 干 干-seal.svg Wikimedia Commons 干 shield seal form; 干 Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg Wikimedia Commons; 干 豦簋 mid Western Zhou shield oracle bone 單 hunting implement paleography; 干 shield 干戈 合集 28059 干衛 Chinese Characters Database
search_audit.outcome: Search returned the exact Commons seal candidate and paleographic/dictionary sources. Opened and inspected the 干-seal.svg page, oracle-style variant page, CUHK paleographic entry, NTU CASE article, and Fudan article. The exact Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg page returned a cache miss. The seal-style redraw is a verified candidate for illustrating a received seal-style form, but not for establishing ancient origin or dating.

search_audit.query: (Commons page link inspection) 干-bronze.svg and 干-oracle.svg
search_audit.outcome: Followed the Commons page’s listed variant links. The bronze file page returned a cache miss; the oracle-style file page opened and identifies a public-domain modern vector redraw, but marks its period as needing verification.

gaps: No physical oracle-bone or bronze glyph image was visually inspected; graphic dating and change are based on the cited paleographic article and dictionary accounts.

The shield interpretation is well supported in the inspected sources, but some proposed Shang identifications remain disputed; Xu Zhongshu’s hunting-implement proposal concerns some oracle-bone forms and is reported rather than independently assessed here.
The Commons seal-style image is a modern vector trace and useful only as an illustration of a received seal-style form. It does not establish the earliest form or shield interpretation.
The precise chronology and semantic links among 干 ‘shield/defend’, 干 ‘offend/violate’, and its use as a simplified spelling of 乾 ‘dry’ and 幹 ‘trunk’ remain unsettled by these checked sources.
